newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Robert Fleming shifts control of 700 mln stg funds.
newsitem.headline: Robert Fleming shifts control of 700 mln stg funds.

text.p: Robert Fleming, the British merchant bank which owns 50 percent of Jardine Fleming, has stripped the Jardine Fleming Investment Management (JFIM) group of almost 700 million stg of retail funds previously managed in Hong Kong, a Hong Kong newspaper reported from London on Sunday.

The funds, from two London-listed investment trusts, would now be managed by Robert Fleming's own asset management team, and several major institutional clients were considering a similar move, the Sunday Morning Post said.
A spokesman for the Hong Kong fund managers, the biggest in the British colony, was not available to comment on Sunday.
Robert Fleming was quoted by the Post as stressing the shift of funds was determined by a build-up of its own fund management capability.

But the paper noted that the move comes as investors seriously question the management systems at Jardine Fleming in the wake of last week's scandal in which the fund manager, the largest in the British colony, was exposed and punished for irregularities including front-running.
Jardine Fleming is jointly owned by the Jardine Matheson and Robert Fleming groups.

A five-month probe by the Investment Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) in London and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) in Hong Kong exposed late allocation of trades, and Jardine Fleming was fined 700,000 sterling.
London-based Jardine Fleming Asset Management lost its authorisation as a result.

The Post said the funds moved back to London included the 640 million stg Fleming Far Eastern Investment Trust and the Fleming Indian Investment Trust with shareholders' funds of about 55 million stg.
